This page explains how the OpenHands Enterprise architecture is put together: the
overall solution, the individual components/services that make it up, and which
external systems are required versus optional.
There are two install paths for OpenHands Enterprise:
VM install (Quick Start): Single VM deployment with all required services
Install with Helm: Install the full OpenHands Enterprise solution in a Kubernetes cluster
For the services, networking, and storage in the Docker Compose stack, see
Docker Compose Architecture.
How It Works
A user’s browser talks to the OpenHands application (server + frontend), which
coordinates with Keycloak for identity, a LiteLLM proxy for LLM calls, and the
Runtime API for spinning up isolated sandboxes where the coding agent actually
runs. Optional services extend this core with scheduled/event-driven automations,
plugins, and richer integrations.
The core loop is:
A user (or a webhook from GitHub, GitLab, Slack, Jira) creates or resumes
a conversation.
The OpenHands app authenticates the request (via Keycloak-issued cookies/tokens) and
asks the Runtime API for a sandbox.
Runtime API assigns a warm (pre-started) or freshly created Runtime pod — an
isolated sandbox running the agent server.
The agent in the sandbox calls out through the LiteLLM proxy to the configured LLM
provider, executes tools (bash, file edits, browser, git), and streams events back to
the app and browser.
The agent can push commits, open PRs/MRs, and comment back on the originating
issue/PR/message through the relevant Git provider or chat/ticketing
integration.
Conversation state and artifacts are persisted to PostgreSQL, Redis (cache/sessions),
and an object store (S3/GCS/MinIO — the “conversation bucket”).
Key Repos
OpenHands Enterprise is assembled from a handful of repositories. Some are open source and shared with the
community edition; others are commercially licensed and make up the enterprise-only layer.
Enterprise Application
RepoLicenseWhat It Provides
OpenHands
Open source (MIT)The web UI, shared by the open source and Enterprise editions.
software-agent-sdk
Open source (MIT)The Python SDK and the agent server that runs inside every sandbox: the agent loop, tools, conversations, and events.
automation
Open source (MIT)The automation service: cron and webhook triggers, dispatch, run history.
enterprise
CommercialThe Enterprise Server: REST/V1 API, conversation orchestration, Git-provider and chat/ticketing integrations, org and user management, and billing.
runtime-api
CommercialThe Runtime API: warm pool and lifecycle of sandbox pods. This is a private repository.
OpenHands-Cloud
CommercialHelm charts and installer packaging used to deploy the whole stack.
Extensions
RepoLicenseWhat It Provides
extensions
Open source (MIT)The public registry of skills, plugins, and automations that agents load.
Documentation
RepoWhat It Provides
docs
This documentation site.
enterprise-cookbook
Code examples and tutorials for OpenHands Enterprise (MIT).
How They Fit Together
OpenHands-Cloud
packages and deploys the other components onto Kubernetes (or a single VM through the
installer).
OpenHands
supplies the web UI, which the Enterprise Server serves to users alongside its own API.
enterprise
is the control plane. It authenticates users, receives webhooks, and asks
runtime-api
for a sandbox for each conversation.
runtime-api
keeps warm sandbox pods ready and starts them from the agent-server image built from
software-agent-sdk
.
software-agent-sdk
is what actually runs in each sandbox: the agent loop that calls the LLM and executes
tools, streaming events back to the Enterprise Server.
automation
triggers agent runs on a schedule or from events. Each run executes in a sandbox, like an
interactive conversation.
extensions
supplies the skills, plugins, and automation templates that agents and the Plugin Directory use.
Components And Services
Core Components
These are present in every deployment.
ComponentWhat It Does
OpenHands (Enterprise Server)The main app: web UI, REST/V1 API, conversation orchestration, Git-provider webhook receivers/resolvers, billing routes, and org/user management.
KeycloakIdentity provider and SSO broker. Terminates

推理-行动循环 - 查询 LLM，基于对话历史生成下一步行动

并返回

该示例展示了一个两阶段工作流程，其中一个自定义规划 Agent（具有只读工具）分析任务并创建结构化计划，然后由一个执行 Agent 实现这些计划，并具有完全的编辑功能。

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Planning Agent Workflow Example
This example demonstrates a two-stage workflow:
1. Planning Agent: Analyzes the task and creates a detailed implementation plan
2. Execution Agent: Implements the plan with full editing capabilities
The task: Create a Python web scraper that extracts article titles and URLs
from a news website, handles rate limiting, and saves results to JSON.
"""
import os
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from pydantic import SecretStr
from openhands.sdk import LLM, Conversation
from openhands.sdk.llm import content_to_str
from openhands.tools.preset.default import get_default_agent
from openhands.tools.preset.planning import get_planning_agent
def get_event_content(event):
"""Extract content from an event."""
if hasattr(event, "llm_message"):
return "".join(content_to_str(event.llm_message.content))
return str(event)
"""Run the planning agent workflow example."""
# Create a temporary workspace
workspace_dir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
print(f"Working in: {workspace_dir}")
# Configure LLM
api_key = os.getenv("LLM_API_KEY")
assert api_key is not None, "LLM_API_KEY environment variable is not set."
model = os.getenv("LLM_MODEL", "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929")
base_url = os.getenv("LLM_BASE_URL")
llm = LLM(
model=model,
base_url=base_url,
api_key=SecretStr(api_key),
usage_id="agent",
)
# Task description
task = """
Create a Python web scraper with the following requirements:
- Scrape article titles and URLs from a news website
- Handle HTTP errors gracefully with retry logic
- Save results to a JSON file with timestamp
- Use requests and BeautifulSoup for scraping
Do NOT ask for any clarifying questions. Directly create your implementation plan.
"""
print("=" * 80)
print("PHASE 1: PLANNING")
print("=" * 80)
# Create Planning Agent with read-only tools
planning_agent = get_planning_agent(llm=llm)
# Create conversation for planning
planning_conversation = Conversation(
agent=planning_agent,
workspace=str(workspace_dir),
)
# Run planning phase
print("Planning Agent is analyzing the task and creating implementation plan...")
planning_conversation.send_message(
f"Please analyze this web scraping task and create a detailed "
f"implementation plan:\n\n{task}"
)
planning_conversation.run()
print("\n" + "=" * 80)
print("PLANNING COMPLETE")
print("=" * 80)
print(f"Implementation plan saved to: {workspace_dir}/PLAN.md")
print("\n" + "=" * 80)
print("PHASE 2: EXECUTION")
print("=" * 80)
# Create Execution Agent with full editing capabilities
execution_agent = get_default_agent(llm=llm, cli_mode=True)
# Create conversation for execution
execution_conversation = Conversation(
agent=execution_agent,
workspace=str(workspace_dir),
)
# Prepare execution prompt with reference to the plan file
execution_prompt = f"""
Please implement the web scraping project according to the implementation plan.
The detailed implementation plan has been created and saved at: {workspace_dir}/PLAN.md
Please read the plan from PLAN.md and implement all components according to it.
Create all necessary files, implement the functionality, and ensure everything
works together properly.
"""
print("Execution Agent is implementing the plan...")
execution_conversation.send_message(execution_prompt)
execution_conversation.run()
# Get the last message from the conversation
execution_result = execution_conversation.state.events[-1]
print("\n" + "=" * 80)
print("EXECUTION RESULT:")
print("=" * 80)
print(get_event_content(execution_result))
print("\n" + "=" * 80)
print("WORKFLOW COMPLETE")
print("=" * 80)
print(f"Project files c

collected_items.content:
Agent Canvas

The self-hosted developer control center for coding agents and automations.

Run OpenHands, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Pi, OpenCode, or any ACP-compatible agent across local, remote, and cloud backends.

Quickstart | Docs | Self-Hosting | ACP Agents | Automations | Slack

OpenHands Agent Canvas turns your coding agents into a self-hosted, always-on engineering team. It's a developer control center for starting conversations and automating everyday tasks — like generating reports that publish to Slack or automatically decomposing GitHub issues into tasks. It runs locally on your machine by default, but can connect to multiple “agent backends”, e.g. running agents in Docker containers, on VMs, or within your company infrastructure. You can optionally choose to run agents on OpenHands Cloud or OpenHands Enterprise infrastructure. Agent Canvas runs the open source OpenHands agent out-of-the-box, but can use third-party agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Pi, and OpenCode. | | | | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | [**Self-host your way**](https://docs.openhands.dev/openhands/usage/agent-canvas/backend-setup/vm) | Run agents locally, in Docker, on VMs, or anywhere you can run an agent server backend | | [**Switch between different backends**](https://docs.openhands.dev/openhands/usage/agent-canvas/backends) | Switch between local, remote, and cloud agents without losing focus | | [**Create automations**](https://docs.openhands.dev/openhands/usage/agent-canvas/prebuilt-automations) | Create automations and workflows that integrate with Slack, GitHub, Linear, and more. Run on a schedule or in response to webhook events | | [**Integrate with the tools you use**](https://docs.openhands.dev/openhands/usage/agent-canvas/prebuilt-automations) | Connect your automations with third-party services like Slack, GitHub, Notion, and more to automate workflows | | [**Bring your own model**](https://docs.openhands.dev/openhands/usage/settings/llm-settings#llm-profiles) | Use with any LLM | | [**Use with any agent**](https://docs.openhands.dev/openhands/usage/agent-canvas/acp-agents) | Use with OpenHands, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Pi, OpenCode, or any agent with Agent-Client Protocol (ACP). | If you have questions or feedback, please open a GitHub issue or join the [#proj-agent-canvas channel in Slack](https://openhands.dev/joinslack). ## Quickstart You can install OpenHands to run agents on any machine: on your laptop, on a dedicated computer like a Mac Mini, or on a server in the cloud. The most powerful way to run OpenHands is on a server in the cloud. This allows your agents to continue running even when your laptop is shut, and makes it easier to trigger your agents through third-party services like Slack, GitHub, and Datadog. See [SELF_HOSTING.md](docs/SELF_HOSTING.md) for details, especially with respect to security hardening. Notably, you can run the backend in _multiple different environments_, and switch between them from the same Agent Canvas frontend. E.g. you can share an Agent Server with your team for agents doing code review and dependency updates, then have your personal agents running on your laptop. ### Option 1: Without a Sandbox > [!WARNING] > This runs the agent-server directly on the machine you're installing on — the agent will have full access to your filesystem! **Prerequisites**: [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) 24 or later, `uv` ```sh npm install -g @openhands/agent-canvas agent-canvas ``` The `agent-canvas` command starts the full local stack by default. You can also split it when you want to run pieces separately: ```sh agent-canvas --frontend-only # static frontend + ingress only agent-canvas --backend-only # agent server + automation backend + ingress only ``` ### Option 2: With a Docker Sandbox Install Docker Desktop on macOS/Windows, or Docker Engine/Docker Desktop on Linux. Windows users can follow the [PowerShell quickstart](./README.windows.md). The steps below are for macOS and Linux. A named Docker volume stores settings, secrets, and conversations; projects are mounted at `/projects`. **1. Prepare a workspace** ```sh export PROJECTS_PATH="$HOME/projects" # directory containing your project folders mkdir -p "$PROJECTS_PATH" ``` On **Linux Docker Engine**, uid 10001 inside the container must be able to read and write the workspace and its existing files. Grant that user access using appropriate ownership or ACLs for your system. For a dedicated workspace you are comfortable sharing with all local users, the following is another option: ```sh find "$PROJECTS_PATH" -type d -exec chmod a+rwX {} + find "$PROJECTS_PATH" -type f -exec chmod a+rw {} + ``` These commands grant all host users access to the workspace. Keep it separate from `~/.openhands` and other sensitive data. Docker Desktop on macOS/Windows handles bind-mount permissions, so those commands are normally unnecessary. **2. Start Agent Canvas** ```sh docker run -it --rm \ -p 127.0.0.1:8000:8000 \ -e AGENT_CANVAS_ALLOW_LAN_SESSION_KEY=true \ -v openhands-state:/home/openhands/.openhands \ -v "${PROJECTS_PATH}:/projects" \ ghcr.io/openhands/agent-canvas:1.46.0 # x-release-please-version ``` Open [http://localhost:8000/canvas](http://localhost:8000/canvas). Reuse `openhands-state` to retain state across container removals. A fresh volume does not contain existing `~/.openhands` data; inspect or back it up with `docker volume inspect openhands-state`.

Introduction - OpenHands Docs
Documentation Index
Fetch the complete documentation index at: /llms.txt

Assistant
Responses are generated using AI and may contain mistakes.
Contact support
OpenHands is an open platform for running AI coding agents across real engineering work. Run agents in conversations,
automate them with schedules and events, extend them with skills, plugins, and MCP servers, and build your own agents
with the Software Agent SDK. Use any LLM, or connect an existing coding agent such as Claude Code or Codex.
We’d love for you to join the community on Slack.
Choose a Product
ProductUse It WhenWhere Agents Run
Agent CanvasYou want a free, open-source workspace on your own machine or serverYour laptop, a VM, Docker, or another backend you connect
OpenHands CloudYou want to start without installing anythingHosted sandboxes at app.all-hands.dev
OpenHands EnterpriseYour organization needs self-hosting, access control, and governanceYour own infrastructure
Software Agent SDKYou want to build agents or embed them in your own toolsYour code, or an Agent Server you deploy
We recommend starting with Agent Canvas or
OpenHands Cloud. See the Quick Start.
How the Products Fit Together
Every product runs agents with the Software Agent SDK. Agent Canvas, OpenHands Cloud, and OpenHands Enterprise share
the same Agent Canvas interface and differ in where the backend runs and who manages it.
Agent Server runs the agent, its tools, and its conversations. It’s part of the Software Agent SDK.
Automation Server runs automations on a schedule or in response to events.
OpenHands Cloud and Enterprise add accounts, sandboxes, integrations, and administration on top of Agent Server
and Automation Server.
Agent Canvas
Agent Canvas is the open-source workspace for running agents. Use it to run
several conversations in parallel, connect agents such as Claude Code or Codex through the Agent Client Protocol, and
create automations.
Install Agent Canvas with npm, npx, or Docker, or try the desktop app, which is in preview. By default, Agent Canvas
starts a backend on your machine. You can also connect it to a VM, Docker, or OpenHands Cloud.
Install Agent Canvas or
view the source.
OpenHands Cloud
OpenHands Cloud is the free hosted version of OpenHands. It runs the same
application as OpenHands Enterprise, with Agent Canvas, for a single user. Cloud includes hosted sandboxes, Git and
Slack integrations, and public webhook URLs for event automations. OpenHands Cloud limits how many conversations you
can run.
Sign in to OpenHands Cloud.
OpenHands Enterprise
OpenHands Enterprise runs on your own infrastructure. It adds organizations, roles, single
sign-on, service accounts, budgets, and built-in integrations such as GitHub, Jira Data Center, and Azure DevOps. Use
Docker Compose for trials and the Teams plan, and Kubernetes for production.
Manage your license, subscription, and support in Customer Center. Learn more
at openhands.dev/enterprise.
Software Agent SDK and Agent Server
The Software Agent SDK is a Python library for building agents that work with code. The same repository
contains Agent Server, which exposes agent execution, conversations, tools, and workspaces through REST and WebSocket
APIs.
Get started with the SDK or
view the source.
Features in Every Product
These guides apply to Agent Canvas, OpenHands Cloud, and OpenHands Enterprise. Each guide notes where a product
differs.
Automations: Run agents on a schedule or in response to events.
Skills, Plugins, and MCP: Give agents
knowledge and tools.
LLM Configuration: Choose a model and provider.

Each public repository includes its own license. Check the repository you use or modify instead of assuming one
license applies to the entire ecosystem.
Legacy
The OpenHands CLI is no longer actively maintained. The legacy local GUI
launched with
openhands serve
is deprecated. For a maintained local installation, use
Agent Canvas.
The archived
OpenHands/legacy
repository preserves the previous backend and
runtime source for reference.

join us on Slack.

Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard that allows OpenHands to communicate with external tool servers, extending the agent’s capabilities with custom tools, specialized data processing, external API access, and more. MCP is based on the open standard defined at modelcontextprotocol.io.
How MCP Works
When OpenHands starts, it:
Reads the MCP configuration
Connects to configured servers (SSE, SHTTP, or stdio)
Registers tools provided by these servers with the agent
Routes tool calls to appropriate MCP servers during execution

Install Agent Canvas - OpenHands Docs
Documentation Index

Contact support
Quick Start
Install Agent Canvas with npm and start the full local stack:
npm install -g @openhands/agent-canvas
agent-canvas
Agent Canvas starts on
http://localhost:8000
; open that URL manually if your browser does not. Then follow First Time Setup to configure a model and open a workspace. If installation or startup fails, see Verify Prerequisites.
If you would rather not install npm packages, prefer an installer with bundled Node.js and
uv
, or want a sandboxed setup, see More Install Options below.
Treat agents and ACP processes as untrusted: they can run shell commands and read or write files with your user account’s permissions. Agent Canvas is the client and does not isolate them — use a container, sandbox, or VM for a tighter boundary, and review VM / Self-Hosted Installation before exposing backend services to a network you do not control.
More Install Options
The
agent-canvas
launcher runs the Canvas client with Agent Server, Automation Server, and ingress as an all-in-one local stack. Use npm or npx for direct local execution, or Docker for a containerized stack with explicit project mounts. You can also run the client separately and connect it to an existing backend.
MethodUse It WhenWhat The Agent Can Access
Desktop app (preview)You want an installer with bundled Node.js and
uv
. Go to macOS, Windows, or Linux instructions.The default local backend runs directly on your machine and can work in local workspaces you open.
npm local installYou want the quickest local browser setup.Runs directly on your machine and can work in local workspaces you open.
DockerYou want a local sandbox with clearer file boundaries.Runs inside a container and can access mounted project directories.
npxYou want to try Agent Canvas without installing the package globally.Runs directly on your machine and can work in local workspaces you open.
VM / self-hostedYou want an always-on backend, stronger hardware, or a team-accessible server.Runs on the VM or dedicated host you configure.
From sourceYou are contributing to Agent Canvas or changing the frontend/backend stack.Runs your local development checkout.
For an installer, choose the desktop preview below. For a browser setup, use
npx
for a quick first run or npm for a reusable
agent-canvas
command. Use Docker when you specifically want sandboxing.
Desktop App (Preview Build)
The desktop app is an early preview for user testing. It bundles Node.js and
uv
, starts its local backend automatically, and does not require you to install npm packages, clone the source, or keep a terminal open. Skip the command-line prerequisites and installation sections below.
Preview builds may have rough edges. The macOS app is not yet signed with an Apple Developer ID or notarized, so Gatekeeper may block it; see desktop troubleshooting. Windows may show a SmartScreen prompt. Current installers support Apple silicon and Intel Macs, and x64 Windows and Linux.
Download the file for your operating system from the Assets list on the latest OpenHands release. Replace
<version>
in the filenames below with the release version. Older builds are on the releases page.
macOS
Download
OpenHands-Agent-Canvas-<version>-universal.dmg
from the latest release assets.
Open the disk image and drag OpenHands Agent Canvas to Applications.
Launch OpenHands Agent Canvas from Applications.
The universal disk image includes Node.js and
uv
for both Apple silicon and Intel Macs.
Windows
Download
OpenHands-Agent-Canvas-Setup-<version>.exe
from the latest release assets.
Run the installer. If Windows SmartScreen prompts you, confirm that the installer came from the official OpenHands release before continuing.
Launch OpenHands Agent Canvas from the Start menu.
Linux
Choose a package from the latest release assets:
AppImage: Download
OpenHands.Agent.Canvas-<version>.AppImage
, make it executable in your file manager’s permissions or with
chmod +x
, then run the file.
Debian / Ubuntu: Download
agent-canvas_<version>_amd64.deb
, install it with your package manager (for example,
sudo apt install ./agent-canvas_<version>_amd64.deb
), then launch OpenHands Agent Canvas from your applications menu.
First Launch
During startup, select Show details to view and copy the live startup log if startup takes longer than expected or fails. Once the app opens, follow First Time Setup to configure a model and open a workspace.
The desktop app can also run conversations in DigitalOcean sandboxes. See DigitalOcean Managed Agents.

Agent Canvas Overview - OpenHands Docs
Documentation Index
Fetch the complete documentation index at: /llms.txt
Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.
Skip to main content
Assistant
Responses are generated using AI and may contain mistakes.
Contact support
Agent Canvas is an open-source control surface for agentic work. From one place, you can manage conversations, files, terminals, model configuration, backends, and automations.
The browser interface connects to one or more backends that run the agent and its tools. By default, that backend runs on your machine, but you can instead use Docker, a VM, Modal, or OpenHands Cloud. The LLM models can run locally, through a provider API or be accessed through an ACP agent.
When To Use Agent Canvas
Choose the path that matches where and how you want your agents to run:
Install Agent Canvas
Run OpenHands locally in a browser.
Use Docker
Use a sandboxed local environment with mounted project directories.
VM / Self-Hosted
Run agents on an always-on machine you control.
Cloud Backend
Connect to managed cloud sandboxes.
ACP Agents
Use Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, or another ACP agent.
Desktop Preview
Test a preview build of the native desktop app.
How Agent Canvas Works
Agent Canvas is the browser client. It connects to backend services that own execution and persistent state:
ConceptWhat It MeansWhy It Matters
Browser UIThe web interface you open in your browser.This is where you chat, inspect files, manage settings, and configure automations.
BackendThe agent server that runs conversations, tools, settings, secrets, and automations.This determines where the agent runs and what machine or sandbox it can access.
WorkspaceThe folder, repository, container mount, or cloud sandbox the agent works in.This determines which files the agent can read and write.
Agent and modelThe OpenHands agent or an ACP agent, plus the model credentials it uses.This determines which LLM or provider receives conversation context and powers the agent.
The
agent-canvas
launcher can package the client and backend services into one local stack. You can also run the client separately and connect it to services on a VM, in Docker or Kubernetes, or through OpenHands Cloud or OpenHands Enterprise.
See Agent Canvas Architecture for the complete service and deployment model.
Switching backends switches the environment the agent is using. For details on how conversations and workspaces remain separate, see Conversations and Backends.
Enterprise License Warnings
On an instance-locked OpenHands Enterprise Canvas, check the banner at the top of the page for license warnings, such as a missing or expired license or an upcoming trial end. The banner appears only when the instance reports a relevant status. It does not appear for a license in good standing, when enforcement is off, or when the instance does not provide a supported license status route.
Choosing A Trust Boundary
Before installing, decide where you want the agent to run and what files it should be able to access.
SetupTrust BoundaryBest For
npm local installRuns directly on your machine. The agent server can operate on the local filesystem.Fastest local setup when you trust the machine and understand the file access.
DockerRuns inside a container and only sees the directories you mount.Local sandboxing and clearer file boundaries.
VM or dedicated machineRuns on the remote host you control.Always-on agents, heavier compute, team-shared backends, or personal/work separation.
OpenHands CloudRuns in managed OpenHands Cloud sandboxes.Cloud execution without maintaining your own machine or VM backend.
Agent Canvas can run agents that execute shell commands, read files, write files, and use connected tools. Only connect a backend to files, secrets, and networks that you are willing to let the agent use.
What Happens When You Close the Terminal?
For a local npm or npx installation, closing the terminal stops the Agent Canvas process, so the browser UI can no longer use its local backend. Start Agent Canvas again with the same command to continue. A Docker container, VM, or cloud backend continues running until that backend is stopped.
See Install to restart Agent Canvas and Troubleshooting if the browser cannot reconnect.
Model Access
Agent Canvas supports several model access patterns:
Direct provider key — enter an API key from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, or another supported provider.
OpenHands LLM API key — use an OpenHands LLM API key for verified hosted models.
ACP agent subscription login — use a signed-in provider, such as Claude Code, Codex, or Gemini, when the backend runs on the same machine as that login.
Local or OpenAI-compatible provider — connect providers such as Ollama, LM Studio, LiteLLM, or a compatible gateway through model settings.
See Configure a Model, Manage LLM Profiles, and ACP Agents for details.
Customize Your Agent
After the first conversation, choose the extension point that matches you

pattern_catalog.name: single_agent
pattern_catalog.description: 单个 LLM 配合工具集，适用于任务边界清晰的场景

pattern_catalog.name: multi_agent_hierarchical
pattern_catalog.description: Planner-Worker 模式，规划 Agent 分解任务，执行 Agent 完成子任务

pattern_catalog.name: multi_agent_peer
pattern_catalog.display_name: 多 Agent 对等协作式
pattern_catalog.description: 多个专业领域 Agent 平级协作，通过共享上下文或消息传递交换信息、相互校验

pattern_catalog.name: multi_agent_swarm
pattern_catalog.description: 去中心化或轻量协调的 Agent 协作网络，支持基于任务和环境的动态转交 (Handoff) 与动态扩缩容

pattern_catalog.name: agent_pipeline
pattern_catalog.description: 任务按固定阶段线性或有向无环图 (DAG) 顺序流转，每个阶段由专有 Agent 负责

pattern_catalog.name: agent_loop
pattern_catalog.description: 基于目标驱动的 ReAct 或 Plan-Execute-Reflect 持续迭代循环，直至达到终止条件

pattern_catalog.name: sliding_window_fifo
pattern_catalog.description: 基于固定 Token 预算或消息条数维护窗口，丢弃最久的历史记录，仅保留最新上下文

pattern_catalog.name: hierarchical_recursive_summary
pattern_catalog.description: 当上下文达到容量阈值时，自动调用模型对早期交互进行结构化压缩与摘要提炼

pattern_catalog.name: rag_dynamic_retrieval
pattern_catalog.description: 将海量历史记录、知识库或代码库切分向量化，根据当前上下文动态召回相关片段按需装载

pattern_catalog.name: prefix_kv_cache_reuse
pattern_catalog.description: 规范化排列上下文，将固定的 System Prompt、工具定义与知识前缀集中前置，最大化复用 KV Cache

pattern_catalog.name: structured_scratchpad_isolation
pattern_catalog.display_name: 结构化工作区与暂存隔离
pattern_catalog.description: 划分独立的命名空间分区（如目标、步骤计划、参考资料、临时便签），保持上下文整洁

pattern_catalog.name: hybrid_tiered_memory
pattern_catalog.display_name: 分层多级混合记忆系统
pattern_catalog.description: 构建包含工作记忆、情节记忆与长期语义概念记忆的三级认知记忆网络

pattern_catalog.name: single_model_static
pattern_catalog.description: 系统全量请求统一路由至单一固定模型，架构最简

pattern_catalog.name: capability_tier_routing
pattern_catalog.description: 依据任务预估复杂度与推理要求，在轻量模型与旗舰模型之间按需动态分流

pattern_catalog.name: intent_semantic_routing
pattern_catalog.description: 基于用户意图的语义特征与分类标签，将请求路由至领域微调或垂直专用模型

pattern_catalog.name: cascade_fallback_routing
pattern_catalog.description: 优先调用低成本或本地模型，若输出校验失败、超时或限流，自动回退到备选大模型

pattern_catalog.name: speculative_draft_routing
pattern_catalog.description: 轻量模型快速生成初稿或补全建议，大模型进行并行校验或增量精修

pattern_catalog.name: ensemble_mixture_routing
pattern_catalog.description: 并行分发给多个不同厂商的基座模型，再由聚合模型进行整合、评判与共识融合

pattern_catalog.name: function_calling_schema
pattern_catalog.description: 通过标准 JSON Schema 描述工具元数据，由 LLM 原生输出符合 Schema 的结构化调用参数

pattern_catalog.name: react_tool_interleaving
pattern_catalog.description: 交替进行思考 (Thought)、行动 (Action) 与观察 (Observation)，根据前序工具返回值动态推导后续调用

pattern_catalog.name: mcp_protocol_standard
pattern_catalog.description: 基于开放标准协议 (Model Context Protocol) 统一接入本地与远程工具及数据源

pattern_catalog.display_name: 代码解释器与沙箱即工具
